code: units <- list(   demand_units = "requests",   demand_period = "one_reference_period",   supply_units = "service_slots",   supply_period = "one_reference_period",   travel_units = "minutes" )  # Travel minutes between 80 origins and 40 facilities on a wavy strip origin_x <- seq(2, 58, length.out = 80) origin_y <- 8 * sin(seq_len(80) * 0.73) facility_x <- seq(4, 56, length.out = 40) facility_y <- 7 * sin(seq_len(40) * 1.31) travel <- sqrt(   outer(origin_x, facility_x, "-")^2 + outer(origin_y, facility_y, "-")^2 ) + 2 dimnames(travel) <- list(paste0("origin", 1:80), paste0("facility", 1:40))  # Demand at each origin and supply at each facility demand <- setNames(80 + 35 * (1 + sin(seq_len(80) * 0.23)), rownames(travel)) supply <- setNames(rep(c(5, 7, 6, 8, 9), 8), colnames(travel))  # True choice probabilities under the CLM truth <- c(sigma = 12, v0 = 45) attraction <- exp(-travel^2 / (2 * truth[["sigma"]]^2)) *   rep(supply, each = length(demand)) probability <- attraction / (rowSums(attraction) + truth[["v0"]])  # Observed facility totals: independent Poisson counts around the truth set.seed(2490001) observed <- setNames(rpois(40, colSums(probability * demand)), names(supply))  # Fit the CLM to the facility totals data <- prep_data(demand, supply, travel, metadata = units) result <- spax(data, spec_clm(), observed = obs_totals(observed)) rbind(truth = truth, estimate = coef(result)) sigma       v0 truth    12.00000 45.00000 estimate 13.27969 48.57531

code: # Demand and travel grids at `factor` times the native cell width at_resolution <- function(factor) {   # Native grid: unchanged   if (factor == 1) return(list(demand = pop, travel = travel_grid))    # Finer grid: split residents evenly, copy the parent's travel times   if (factor < 1) {     split <- round(1 / factor)     return(list(       demand = disagg(pop, split) / split^2,       travel = disagg(travel_grid, split)     ))   }    # Coarser grid: add up residents, take resident-weighted mean minutes   demand <- aggregate(pop, factor, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)   minutes <- aggregate(travel_grid * pop, factor, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE) /     demand   list(demand = demand, travel = minutes) }  factors <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 4) grids <- lapply(factors, at_resolution) e2sfca_spec <- spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10))  # The E2SFCA index on one resolution's grids index_at <- function(grid) {   resolution_data <- prep_data(     grid$demand,     gp,     grid$travel,     id_col = "practice",     supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg"   )   spax(resolution_data, e2sfca_spec) }  # Median elapsed seconds of three runs at each resolution seconds <- sapply(grids, function(grid) {   median(replicate(3, system.time(index_at(grid))[["elapsed"]])) })  results <- lapply(grids, index_at) # The native surface and residents, one value per native cell native <- 1000 * values(results[[2]]$accessibility, mat = FALSE) residents <- values(pop, mat = FALSE)  # One table row per resolution summary_row <- function(level) {   # This surface on the native grid   on_native <- resample(results[[level]]$accessibility, pop, method = "near")   on_native <- 1000 * values(on_native, mat = FALSE)    # Residents and cell area on this resolution's own grid   demand <- values(grids[[level]]$demand, mat = FALSE)   area <- values(cellSize(grids[[level]]$demand, unit = "km"), mat = FALSE)    # Index per 1,000 on its own grid, and the change from the native surface   own <- 1000 * values(results[[level]]$accessibility, mat = FALSE)   change <- abs(on_native / native - 1)    data.frame(     factor = factors[level],     cell_km2 = round(mean(area[!is.na(demand)]), 2),     cells = sum(!is.na(demand)),     seconds = seconds[level],     mean_per_1000 = round(weighted.mean(own, demand, na.rm = TRUE), 3),     median_change_pct = round(       100 * median(change[!is.na(residents)], na.rm = TRUE),       1     ),     mean_change_pct = round(       100 * weighted.mean(change, residents, na.rm = TRUE),       1     )   ) }  comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(factors), summary_row)) comparison factor cell_km2 cells seconds mean_per_1000 median_change_pct mean_change_pct 1    0.5     0.14 27648   0.423         0.575               0.0             0.0 2    1.0     0.55  6912   0.043         0.575               0.0             0.0 3    2.0     2.20  1829   0.009         0.575               1.8             1.4 4    4.0     8.79   506   0.006         0.575               3.3             2.5 # Step 2. area adds ratios practices around , weighted . village leans better-supplied north practice scores highest, 0.99 GP FTE per 1,000 residents. coast leans south practice scores lowest, 0.58. code: # Residents of three areas, and GP FTE at two practices demand <- c(village = 1000, town = 4000, coast = 2000) supply <- c(north = 3, south = 2)  # Weight of each practice (columns) for each area (rows) weights <- rbind(   village = c(north = 1.0, south = 0.1),   town    = c(north = 0.5, south = 0.5),   coast   = c(north = 0.1, south = 1.0) ) weights north south village   1.0   0.1 town      0.5   0.5 coast     0.1   1.0 # For each practice: residents times weight, summed over the areas gathered <- colSums(weights * demand) gathered north south   3200  4100 # GP FTE per 1,000 weighted residents ratio <- supply / gathered round(1000 * ratio, 2) north south   0.94  0.49 # For each area: practice ratios times weight, summed over the practices index <- drop(weights %*% ratio) round(1000 * index, 2) village    town   coast     0.99    0.71    0.58 # Residents times the index, summed over the areas sum(index * demand) [1] 5

code: library(spax) library(terra) library(sf) library(dplyr)  gp <- cornwall_gp |>   filter(!scilly) |>   st_drop_geometry() pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")[[gp$practice]] # Keep cells with a travel time to every mainland practice pop <- trim(mask(pop, sum(travel_grid))) travel_grid <- crop(travel_grid, pop) grid_data <- prep_data(pop, gp, travel_grid, id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")  # The E2SFCA index with a Gaussian decay of travel scale 10 minutes fca <- spax(grid_data, spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10)))  # Mainland Cornwall's outline, in the grid's longitude and latitude outline <- cornwall_lsoa |>   filter(!scilly) |>   st_union() |>   vect()  plot(   1000 * fca$accessibility,   axes = FALSE,   col = hcl.colors(50, "viridis"),   main = "E2SFCA index, GP FTE per 1,000 residents" ) lines(outline, lwd = 0.6)

title: Spatial Accessibility and Allocation Modeling

Registration local. outside weight v0 acts like practice 0.03 GP FTE next door every area. model places 0.54% registered residents practices outside mainland Cornwall, 0.91% observed. fit uses counts mainland practices. residents register? shows give area’s known outside count .

code: # West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa) areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ] gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp) gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ] travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice] inputs <- prepare_allocation(stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa),                              stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice),                              travel) model <- clm_allocation(inputs, fit_v0 = TRUE)  # Registrations of these residents at these practices flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &                           cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]  # Fit to the practice totals. Without starts, the search finds starts and # bounds from the data, and the loss must be named totals <- sapply(split(flows$patients, flows$practice), sum) fit <- fit_allocation(model, totals, loss = "poisson") fit #> <allocation fit> 3 starts, selected scan1 #> eligible starts: 3 / 3 #> selected start: scan1 #> starts: default search, 45 of 45 grid points, loss poisson #> loss disagreement: FALSE; parameter disagreement: FALSE #>  start     loss eligible optim_convergence solver_converged residual seconds #>  scan1 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.017 #>  scan2 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.029 #>  scan3 -1200843     TRUE                 0             TRUE        0   0.025 #>  boundary   status                                    optim_message #>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL #>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL #>     FALSE eligible CONVERGENCE: NORM OF PROJECTED GRADIENT <= PGTOL #>  solver_message log_parameter_gap     loss_gap #>       converged      0.000000e+00 0.000000e+00 #>       converged      8.566946e-07 0.000000e+00 #>       converged      6.215664e-06 1.164153e-09 coef(fit) #>     sigma        v0  #> 13.223212  1.001842   # Fit to the flows: a matrix of small areas by practices, 0 where none. Demand # counts every registered resident, so the residents registered elsewhere are # known: they are one more column, "(outside)", fitted by the outside option flow_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel)) flow_matrix[cbind(flows$lsoa, flows$practice)] <- flows$patients flow_matrix <- cbind(flow_matrix, "(outside)" = areas$registered - rowSums(flow_matrix)) coef(fit_allocation(model, flow_matrix, output = "flow_outside", loss = "poisson")) #>      sigma         v0  #> 3.97012750 0.09627051   # Starts and bounds of your own: one start per row starts <- rbind(near = c(sigma = 5, v0 = 0.5), far = c(sigma = 30, v0 = 5)) fit_own <- fit_allocation(model, totals, starts = starts,                           lower = c(sigma = 1, v0 = 0.001),                           upper = c(sigma = 100, v0 = 100), loss = "poisson") coef(fit_own) #>     sigma        v0  #> 13.223190  1.001846

title: Declare the Huff model — huff_allocation
code: # Mainland Cornwall: small areas share their registered residents among the # practices in proportion to attractiveness times travel-time decay. areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ]) gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ]) travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice]  # Without an outside option, demand is the residents registered at the # mainland practices demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered_in, areas$lsoa) supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice) inputs <- prepare_allocation(demand, supply, travel)  # Power decay with a fitted attractiveness exponent model <- huff_allocation(inputs)  # Evaluate at given parameters: distance exponent 2, attractiveness # exponent 1 evaluate_allocation(model, c(sigma = 2, beta = 1)) #> <allocation evaluation> #> converged: TRUE #> iterations: 1 #> error: 0 #> residual_norm: 0  # Fit practice totals of registrations from two starts totals <- tapply(cornwall_flows$patients, cornwall_flows$practice, sum) observed <- stats::setNames(numeric(ncol(travel)), colnames(travel)) observed[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))] <-   totals[intersect(names(totals), names(observed))] fit <- fit_allocation(   model, observed,   starts = rbind(a = c(sigma = 1, beta = 0.5), b = c(sigma = 3, beta = 1.5)),   lower = c(sigma = 0.1, beta = 0.05), upper = c(sigma = 10, beta = 5),   loss = "poisson" ) fit$best$theta #>     sigma      beta  #> 1.0415962 0.6062301

code: # West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa) areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ] gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp) gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ] supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)  # Fit on every other small area; predict the others, which lie among them, # so these practices are their real choice set fit_areas <- areas[seq(1, nrow(areas), by = 2), ] held_out <- areas[seq(2, nrow(areas), by = 2), ]  # A fit to the registrations of the fitted areas' residents, with those # registered elsewhere as the outside column (see fit_allocation()) travel <- cornwall_travel[fit_areas$lsoa, gp$practice] flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% fit_areas$lsoa &                           cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ] flow_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel)) flow_matrix[cbind(flows$lsoa, flows$practice)] <- flows$patients flow_matrix <- cbind(flow_matrix,                      "(outside)" = fit_areas$registered - rowSums(flow_matrix)) model <- clm_allocation(prepare_allocation(   stats::setNames(fit_areas$registered, fit_areas$lsoa), supply, travel), fit_v0 = TRUE) fit <- fit_allocation(model, flow_matrix, output = "flow_outside", loss = "poisson")  # The held-out areas: no refit, the fitted values and practice loads are used pred <- predict_allocation(fit, cornwall_travel[held_out$lsoa, gp$practice],                            demand = stats::setNames(held_out$registered, held_out$lsoa),                            outputs = c("rho", "A", "flow")) pred #> <allocation prediction> 42 origins x 15 facilities #>   origins     42 valid #>   demand      42 positive #>   travel      an unknown travel time makes the origin unknown #>   outputs #>     rho   0.147 to 0.9912 (42 of 42 origins) #>     A     0.000187 to 0.001756 (42 of 42 origins) #>     flow  42 origins x 15 facilities #>   values in $outputs; the status of each origin in $validity  # The modeled share of each area's residents at these practices, the share # registered there, and the GP FTE per 1,000 residents attributed to the area held <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% held_out$lsoa &                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ] registered_here <- tapply(held$patients, factor(held$lsoa, levels = held_out$lsoa), sum) head(cbind(contact = pred$outputs$rho,            observed = registered_here / held_out$registered,            fte_per_1000 = 1000 * pred$outputs$A)) #>             contact  observed fte_per_1000 #> E01018861 0.9667815 0.9945088     1.550514 #> E01018863 0.9747945 0.9979242     1.385976 #> E01018865 0.9904890 0.9911318     1.129310 #> E01018868 0.9889620 0.9973118     1.153529 #> E01018870 0.9897772 0.9938229     1.147452 #> E01018872 0.9870558 0.6741517     1.203248 table(pred$validity$status) #>  #> valid  #>    42

title: Prepare data for a spax model — prep_data
code: # Mainland Cornwall: registered residents, GP FTE and travel minutes areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa[!cornwall_lsoa$scilly, ]) gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp[!cornwall_gp$scilly, ]) demand <- stats::setNames(areas$registered, areas$lsoa) supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice) travel <- cornwall_travel[areas$lsoa, gp$practice] prep_data(demand, supply, travel,           metadata = list(demand_units = "registered residents",                           supply_units = "GP FTE", travel_units = "minutes")) #> <spax data> 336 origins (336 active) x 54 facilities #>   demand      604,471 registered residents #>   supply      GP FTE #>   travel      minutes; unknown for 0 active origins #>   policies    missing demand: error; missing travel: error  # Raster data for a floating catchment area index pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel_grid <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif") grid_data <- prep_data(pop, sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp), travel_grid,                        id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg") grid_data #> <spax data> raster 132 x 271 cells x 55 facilities; supply gp_fte_extg #>   demand    1 layer; travel 55 layers #>   note      holds terra rasters: prepare the data again after saveRDS() spax(grid_data, spec_e2sfca(decay = decay_gaussian(sigma = 10))) #> <spax access> E2SFCA, 1 layer on 132 x 271 cells #>  #> Spatial Properties: #> - Resolution: 0.00833333 x 0.00833333 #> - Dimensions: 132 x 271 #>  #> Measures: 1 #> - gp_fte_extg #>  #> Facilities: 55 #>  #> Parameters: #> - Decay function: gaussian (sigma = 10) #> - Demand normalization: identity   # \donttest{ # An allocation model on the mainland grid, fitted to practice totals. Demand # must count the same people as the totals: residents registered with a GP # practice. The grid estimates residents in 2020, fewer than the registered # residents of the mainland small areas, so it is scaled to them and gives # only where they live. mainland <- terra::ext(-6, terra::xmax(pop), terra::ymin(pop), terra::ymax(pop)) pop <- terra::crop(pop, mainland) registered <- pop * sum(areas$registered) /   terra::global(pop, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] travel_mainland <- terra::crop(travel_grid[[gp$practice]], mainland)  # Cells of 2 x 2 grid cells keep the example quick: residents add up and # travel minutes average registered <- terra::aggregate(registered, fact = 2, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE) travel_mainland <- terra::aggregate(travel_mainland, fact = 2, fun = "mean",                                     na.rm = TRUE) d_mainland <- prep_data(registered, gp, travel_mainland,                         id_col = "practice", supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg")  # Registrations of mainland residents at the mainland practices flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% areas$lsoa &                           cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ] totals <- obs_totals(tapply(flows$patients, flows$practice, sum))  # The cells with residents become the origins. The Huff model (power decay, # fitted attractiveness exponent) is well determined by these totals. huff <- spax(d_mainland, spec_huff(), observed = totals) huff #> <spax allocation> Huff model (no outside option) #>   decay       power (sigma = exponent): fit #>   attraction  (kappa * supply)^beta: kappa = 1, beta = fit #>   outside     none #>   data        1,824 origins x 54 facilities #>  #>   parameter  value   status #>   sigma      1.077   fitted #>   beta       0.6154  fitted #>   v0         0       held #>   kappa      1       held #>  #>   selected    scan1 (start 1 of 3); 3 of 3 starts converged #>   boundary    none #>   starts      default search, 15 of 15 grid points, loss poisson  # What the totals say about travel: the fit against no decay check_fit(huff) #> <allocation check> #>     comparator     loss loss_difference contact trip_median trip_p90 #>         fitted -5041836               0       1        11.5       53 #>       no_decay -5038257            3579       1        39.5       85 #>  capacity_only -5038282            3554      NA        39.5       85 #> Trip lengths are one-way, in travel units, weighted by expected flows. #>  #> The fitted allocation reproduces the counts better than both comparators. # }

text: x Single-layer SpatRaster representing spatial distribution. Can either: PMF values sum 1 Raw density values converted PMF (except snap mode) n Integer NULL. Fixed number samples deterministic sampling. specified, overrides probabilistic sampling parameters. size Integer NULL. Population size parameter probability distributions. NULL input density (PMF), rounded total data used. prob Numeric 0 1. Probability parameter sampling methods (e.g., disease prevalence, detection probability). method Character string function specifying sampling method: "poisson": Random size mean size * prob "binomial": Random size binomial(size, prob) "nbinom": Random size negative binomial(size, prob) custom function: Must return vector length iterations iterations Integer. Number realizations generate (default = 1) evolve_prop Numeric 0 1. Controls sample evolution iterations: 1 (default): Independent sampling, new samples iteration 0: new samples, returns first iteration 0 1: Proportion samples evolve iteration seed Integer NULL. Random seed reproducibility replace_0 Logical. TRUE, replaces zero values NA (default = TRUE) snap Logical. TRUE, enters fast mode minimal validation (default = FALSE) ... Additional arguments passed custom sampling function

title: Sample Points from Probability Surface with Multiple Realizations — sample_pmf
code: # Population density on a small grid r <- terra::rast(nrows = 10, ncols = 10) set.seed(1) terra::values(r) <- runif(100) * 100  # Independent samples of 50 cases, five iterations samples1 <- sample_pmf(r, n = 50, iterations = 5)  # Evolving samples: 30% of cases are redrawn at each iteration samples2 <- sample_pmf(r, n = 50, iterations = 5, evolve_prop = 0.3)  # Poisson counts with an expected prevalence of 0.1% samples3 <- sample_pmf(r,   size = 10000,   prob = 0.001,   method = "poisson",   iterations = 10,   evolve_prop = 0.2 )

title: Calculate Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA) accessibility scores — spax_e2sfca
code: # Load example data library(terra) library(sf)  # Cornwall population grid and travel time to each GP practice pop_rast <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")  # Drop geometry for supply data gp <- cornwall_gp |> st_drop_geometry()  # Calculate accessibility with Gaussian decay result <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     method = "gaussian",     sigma = 10 # 10-minute characteristic travel time   ),   demand_normalize = "semi", # Prevent demand inflation   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" )  # Extract and plot accessibility surface plot(result$accessibility, main = "GP Accessibility (E2SFCA)")   # Access facility-level information head(result$facilities) #>       id gp_fte_extg #> 1 L82001   10.298887 #> 2 L82003    4.693333 #> 3 L82004    4.341333 #> 4 L82006    7.973333 #> 5 L82007    2.888800 #> 6 L82008    4.670400  # Compare different decay functions result_exp <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     method = "exponential",     sigma = 0.1   ),   demand_normalize = "semi",   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" )  # Plot both for comparison plot(c(result$accessibility, result_exp$accessibility),   main = c("Gaussian Decay", "Exponential Decay") )   # Two demand groups that compete for the same practices, with a fixed # illustrative split of the population and a decay scale for each group groups <- list(younger = pop_rast * 0.6, older = pop_rast * 0.4) result_groups <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = groups,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(     younger = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 8),     older = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 15)   ),   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" ) names(result_groups$accessibility) #> [1] "gp_fte_extg.younger" "gp_fte_extg.older"   "gp_fte_extg.all"     result_groups$parameters$groups #> [1] "younger" "older"   plot(result_groups$accessibility)

code: # Load example data library(terra) library(sf)  # Cornwall population grid and travel time to each GP practice pop_rast <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif")  # Drop geometry for supply data gp <- cornwall_gp |> st_drop_geometry()  # Attractiveness defaults to the supply measure (GP FTE excluding trainees) result <- spax_huff2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" ) plot(result$accessibility, main = "GP Accessibility (Huff-2SFCA)")   # Another attractiveness, named by practice, with a stronger effect result_gp <- spax_huff2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),   attractiveness = setNames(gp$gp_fte, gp$practice), # all GPs   alpha = 2,   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" )  # Plot both for comparison plot(c(result$accessibility, result_gp$accessibility),   main = c("Attractiveness = supply", "All GPs, alpha = 2") )

code: library(terra) library(sf)  # Cornwall population grid and travel time to each GP practice pop_rast <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif") gp <- cornwall_gp |> st_drop_geometry()  # M2SFCA with Gaussian decay result <- spax_m2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" ) result #> <spax access> M2SFCA, 1 layer on 132 x 271 cells #>  #> Spatial Properties: #> - Resolution: 0.00833333 x 0.00833333 #> - Dimensions: 132 x 271 #>  #> Measures: 1 #> - gp_fte_extg #>  #> Facilities: 55 #>  #> Parameters: #> - Decay function: gaussian (sigma = 10) #> - Demand normalization: identity   # E2SFCA with the same decay, for comparison result_e2 <- spax_e2sfca(   demand = pop_rast,   supply = gp,   distance = travel,   decay_params = list(method = "gaussian", sigma = 10),   id_col = "practice",   supply_cols = "gp_fte_extg" ) plot(c(result_e2$accessibility, result$accessibility),   main = c("E2SFCA", "M2SFCA") )   # The share of the E2SFCA score that M2SFCA keeps: the average decay weight # of the practices in reach, low where they are far away plot(result$accessibility / result_e2$accessibility,   main = "M2SFCA / E2SFCA" )

title: Calculate spatial accessibility scores — spread_access
code: library(terra)  # Cornwall population grid, and Gaussian weights of the travel time to each # GP practice pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif") travel <- read_spax_example("cornwall_gp_travel.tif") weights <- calc_decay(travel, method = "gaussian", sigma = 10)  # Step 1 of E2SFCA: the population each practice reaches, and its GP FTE per # person reached, for GPs excluding GPs in training and for all GPs gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp) gp <- gp[match(names(weights), gp$practice), ] reached <- gather_weighted(pop, weights, simplify = TRUE) ratios <- data.frame(extg = gp$gp_fte_extg / reached, all = gp$gp_fte / reached)  # Step 2: spread the ratios back over the grid with the same weights access <- spread_access(ratios, weights, ratio_cols = c("extg", "all"),                         plot_prefix = "gp_fte_") access #> class       : SpatRaster #> size        : 132, 271, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 0.008333333, 0.008333333  (x, y) #> extent      : -6.40125, -4.142917, 49.85792, 50.95792  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) #> source(s)   : memory #> names       : gp_fte_extg, gp_fte_all #> min values  :    0.000027,    0.00003 #> max values  :    0.007704,   0.007704 plot(access)   # With full_output, the score that each practice adds to each cell as well detail <- spread_access(ratios$extg, weights, full_output = TRUE) names(detail) #> [1] "access_scores" "site_specific"

what: Update Probability Mass Function with Likelihood Surface — update_pmf
title: Update Probability Mass Function with Likelihood Surface — update_pmf
text: Updates spatial probability mass function (PMF) using likelihood surface following Bayesian principles. function combines: Prior: Initial spatial PMF representing prior beliefs Likelihood: Surface showing relative intensity observations Posterior: Updated PMF incorporating prior likelihood Values posterior higher prior probability likelihood high, representing areas supported prior beliefs observed data.

title: Update Probability Mass Function with Likelihood Surface — update_pmf
code: pop <- read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif")  # Group small areas into larger units (LSOA names end in a letter; dropping it # gives the containing MSOA) so every unit covers several grid cells areas <- terra::vect(cornwall_lsoa) areas$msoa <- sub("[A-Z]$", "", areas$name) msoa <- terra::aggregate(areas, by = "msoa", fun = "sum")  # Likelihood from a rate, not a count: the share of residents registered # with a GP outside Cornwall (counts would double-count population) msoa$out_rate <- msoa$sum_registered_out / msoa$sum_registered likelihood <- transform_likelihood(msoa, value_col = "out_rate", template = pop)  # Prior from population; the posterior is proportional to population times # the out-of-area rate prior <- transform_pmf(pop) posterior <- update_pmf(prior, likelihood)
